content.title: About
content.content: Gelatin salad with vegetables is a cold dish where gelatin forms a clear, jelly‑like matrix that holds diced fresh vegetables (cucumber, carrot, bell pepper, radish). It is served chilled, often cut into cubes, and works as a light snack or side.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Gelatin is derived from collagen extracted from animal bones and skin.
The salad is popular in diet cuisine because it is low‑calorie and high in water content.
In Russia similar dishes are called “kholodets with vegetables,” though traditional kholodets is made from meat broth.
Gelatin preserves the shape and color of vegetables, making the dish visually appealing.
The dish is often garnished with fresh herbs and a squeeze of lemon for brightness.

items.title: Rich in collagen
items.content: Gelatin provides hydrolyzed collagen, which supports skin, joint and connective‑tissue health.

items.title: Low‑calorie
items.content: The salad contains minimal fat and few calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Source of vitamins and minerals
items.content: The vegetables supply vitamin C, vitamin A, potassium and dietary fiber.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: High water content in the jelly and vegetables helps maintain body fluid balance.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Gelatin breaks down readily in the stomach, making the dish gentle on the digestive system.

items.title: Gelatin allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to gelatin, especially those sensitive to animal‑derived products.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If the gelatin is prepared with added salt or soy sauce, the sodium level can be high.

items.title: Not suitable for vegetarians/vegans
items.content: Gelatin is made from animal tissues, so the dish is unsuitable for plant‑based diets.

items.title: Vegetable freshness
items.content: Improperly washed or old vegetables can become a source of bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled, cut into cubes or slices. It can be eaten as a standalone appetizer, paired with fish or chicken, or used as a light component of a festive buffet.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Discard if it develops off‑odors or discoloration.
